metadata.title: fix(rbac): unblock self-service public team join for non-admin users
metadata.author: crivetimihai

description:
## Summary

- Add `check_globally` parameter to `require_permission()` decorator to evaluate permissions against global/personal roles without binding to the request's `team_id`
- Apply to team-entry endpoints (`join`, `leave`, `join-request`, `cancel-join-request`) where users need `teams.join` but aren't yet members of the target team
- Add team_id validation to admin cancel-join-request to prevent cross-team cancellation
- Fix two Playwright test bugs (wrong token type, wrong assertion)

Closes #3960

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests: `pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/middleware/test_rbac.py tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_permission_service_token_narrowing.py tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_rbac_cross_team_isolation.py -v` (335 pass)
- [ ] Full unit suite: 15,274 pass, 0 fail
- [ ] Pylint parallel: `make pylint` → 10.00/10
- [ ] Playwright: `test_request_to_join_public_team`, `test_member_leaves_team`, `test_cross_team_tool_not_visible`
- [ ] Manual: non-admin session token → `POST /teams/{public_team}/join` → 200

reviews.author: gandhipratik203
reviews.body:
## Review Notes

### Findings

**1. Medium: `check_globally` drops the route `team_id` before the plugin permission hook runs, which regresses team-aware `HTTP_AUTH_CHECK_PERMISSION` plugins on these endpoints.**

File: `mcpgateway/middleware/rbac.py:627`, `mcpgateway/middleware/rbac.py:657`

Why it matters: the new behavior is correct for built-in RBAC evaluation, but the original target-team context is also the input to plugin authorization. With the current change, plugins receive `team_id=None` for `join`, `leave`, and join-request endpoints, even when the route clearly targets a specific team.

Evidence: `HttpAuthCheckPermissionPayload` explicitly models `team_id` as hook context (`mcpgateway/plugins/framework/hooks/http.py:143`), and the docs describe it as "Team context (if applicable)" (`docs/docs/using/plugins/http-auth-hooks.md:251`).

Suggested fix: preserve the original route `team_id` for plugin hook/audit payloads, and only null it for the internal `PermissionService.check_permission(...)` call.

**2. Medium: the new cross-team cancel guard is missing the deny-path regression test that this security-sensitive fix needs.**

File: `mcpgateway/admin.py:6894`

Why it matters: this PR adds an important check that prevents canceling a join request with a mismatched `team_id`/`request_id` pair, but there is no unit test asserting the new wrong-team path returns `404`.

Evidence: existing cancel tests cover success/failure/exception cases, but not "valid request id, wrong team id" (`tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_admin.py:16798`, `tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_admin_module.py:1179`).

Suggested fix: add a unit test that submits a real `request_id` under the wrong `team_id` and asserts `404`.

**3. Low: the new Playwright JWT helper uses `token_use: str = None`, which should be typed as `Optional[str] = None`.**

File: `tests/playwright/teams/conftest.py:29`

Why it matters: this is only a typing correctness issue, not a runtime bug.

---

### Notes from verification

- The core RBAC intent looks correct. For built-in RBAC, `check_globally=True` does unblock public-team entry flows by avoiding token-team binding on the permission check.
- Verified the default-role path: non-admin users are expected to have global `platform_viewer`, which includes `teams.join`.
- The updated Playwright expectation for cross-team tool access returning `403` matches the current behavior.

### Validation

Reviewed against the PR head in an isolated checkout. Ran targeted unit suites around the changed areas successfully:
- `tests/unit/mcpgateway/middleware/test_rbac.py -k check_globally`
- `tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_admin.py -k 'cancel_join_request or create_join_request or leave_team'`
- `tests/unit/mcpgateway/routers/test_teams.py -k 'request_to_join_team or leave_team'`
- `tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_permission_service_token_narrowing.py`
- `tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_rbac_cross_team_isolation.py`
- `tests/unit/mcpgateway/routers/test_teams_coverage.py`
- `tests/unit/mcpgateway/routers/test_teams_v2.py`

reviews.author: madhav165
reviews.body:
Building on gandhipratik203's Finding 1 — I think the plugin context regression points to a deeper issue worth discussing.

The `check_globally` parameter is working around a permission check that may not need to exist on `join`, `join-request`, and `cancel-join-request` in the first place. `teams.join` is present in every built-in role including `platform_viewer`, which every authenticated user receives globally — so this check can never meaningfully fail for a legitimately authenticated user.

The real authorization on these endpoints is already in the endpoint body and service: `join` and `join-request` validate team visibility and existing membership directly, and `cancel_join_request` in `TeamManagementService` filters by user_email, enforcing ownership.

The suggested change:
- Remove `@require_permission` from `join`, `join-request`, and `cancel-join-request` (three endpoints across two files).
- Keep the decorator on `leave` but revert `check_globally=True` from it — the user is already a member when leaving, so the original team scoping works correctly there and the flag was unnecessary.
- This lets us revert `check_globally` from the decorator entirely, the `**kwargs` additions to the mock decorators, and the three new unit tests.

Finding 1 is resolved at the root rather than by threading route context separately through the plugin payload.

The cross-team cancellation fix in `admin_cancel_join_request` is a genuine improvement and worth keeping regardless.

commits.message:
fix(rbac): unblock self-service public team join for non-admin users

Add `check_globally` parameter to `require_permission()` decorator that
evaluates the permission against global/personal roles only, bypassing
the token-scoping guard in `_get_user_roles()` that discards all roles
when team_id is not in token_teams.

Applied to team-entry endpoints where the user needs `teams.join` but
is not yet a member of the target team:
- POST /teams/{team_id}/join
- POST /admin/teams/{team_id}/leave
- POST /admin/teams/{team_id}/join-request
- DELETE /admin/teams/{team_id}/join-request/{request_id}

Also fixes admin cancel-join-request to validate that the join request
belongs to the team_id in the URL, preventing cross-team cancellation.

Test fixes:
- test_member_leaves_team: use session token instead of public-only JWT
- test_cross_team_tool_not_visible: expect 403 (matches unit test contract)
- Mock decorators accept **kwargs for new parameter

Closes #3960

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
